page.layout: One page of text, single column, with a running head at the top; faint show-through from the reverse page in the right margin (not transcribed). Below the text a catchword-like fragment "In fa-" at the lower right, which is a line-end hyphenated word and belongs to the text.

main_text.p: Nemo se vento nimium secundo< Efferat:vento nimium reflante Nemo desperet:medium sed inter Seruet vtrumque.
Numinis vindex manus in superbos Imminet:pressos releuat:beatus Ille cui multum fauet illa:gaudens Sorte quieta.
main_text.head: Papauer. Docti gerunt semen in capite.
main_text.p: Docta gerat Pallas capitata papauera:namque E cerebro fertur nata fuisse Iouis.
Palladiisque viris(capitis quia femina spargunt, Ingenij gignunt dum monimenta fui) Symbola sint passim capitata papauera:cura Parua fit vt ventris,maxima sed capitis.
main_text.head: De Monimentis lapideis a clarissimo viro D. I.Grutero collectis.
main_text.p: Quid durabilius saxo?quid durius?Esse Quid leuius charta debiliusve potest? Ecce tamen cedunt tenui durissima chartae Sculptorum prisca saxa recusa manu: Artifices istaec quondam posuere periti, Hanc ipsos,Pallas quae facit artifices. Deucalion spargens lapides animauit:at illos, Mi Grutere,legens arte,perire vetas.
main_text.head: Sacra Scriptura arcana scrutari. Pruteni succinum ex Oceano trahentes.
main_text.p: Heu,quantum sumunt operae subeuntque pericli Pruteni,vt promant succina fulua mari! Et vos(o multum coelo dilecta iuuentus, Numinis est cuius mens decorata metu)

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse page and marginal ghosting in the right margin are not transcribed. Faint marginal marks on the left are ignored. Some words of the Latin verse are uncertain at the edges of the scan (e.g. "Nemo se vento nimium secundo" line-end). The text is transcribed as printed in the scan; the first line of the first poem "Nemo se vento" is printed with a long-s-like form and read as "se".
